intro: The PRAM Score is a respiratory scoring tool used in paediatric practice. Preschool Respiratory Assessment Measure - asthma exacerbation severity. It scores 5 criteria and interprets the total across 3 bands, so the number always arrives with the severity it implies rather than on its own. In PediAid each criterion is shown as a labelled option with the weight it carries, so the total can be checked rather than taken on trust.
indications: Grading severity at the bedside in respiratory
Recording an objective severity band in the case notes
Deciding when a total crosses the threshold for escalation
Re-scoring to track whether a child is improving or deteriorating
Checking the exact criteria of a score used infrequently
method: The score sums 5 criteria: Suprasternal retractions; Scalene muscle contraction; Air entry; Wheezing; Oxygen saturation on room air. Totals are then banded: any score - Mild: pRAM 0-3 - mild exacerbation. Inhaled short-acting beta-agonist; usually dischargeable after response; 4 points or more - Moderate: pRAM 4-7 - moderate exacerbation. Frequent bronchodilators plus systemic corticosteroid; observe for response; 8 points or more - Severe: pRAM 8-12 - severe exacerbation. Continuous bronchodilators, systemic steroid, consider magnesium sulphate, oxygen and admission/HDU.
guidelineRefs: Total range 0-12. Validated for children aged roughly 2-17 years.
Source: Chalut DS, Ducharme FM, Davis GM. The Preschool Respiratory Assessment Measure (PRAM). J Pediatr 2000;137:762-8.

faqs.q: How many criteria does the PRAM Score use?
faqs.a: 5. They are Suprasternal retractions; Scalene muscle contraction; Air entry; Wheezing; Oxygen saturation on room air.

faqs.q: What do the bands of the PRAM Score mean?
faqs.a: The total is interpreted as: any score - Mild: pRAM 0-3 - mild exacerbation. Inhaled short-acting beta-agonist; usually dischargeable after response; 4 points or more - Moderate: pRAM 4-7 - moderate exacerbation. Frequent bronchodilators plus systemic corticosteroid; observe for response; 8 points or more - Severe: pRAM 8-12 - severe exacerbation. Continuous bronchodilators, systemic steroid, consider magnesium sulphate, oxygen and admission/HDU.

faqs.q: Does the score replace clinical judgement?
faqs.a: No. It is a structured way to record and communicate severity. A clinician concerned about a child should act on that concern regardless of the total.
